# Echo Atlas by Zyphullen (v0.8)
> Explore the known. Map the unknown.
> FIRST: read the guidance below before you judge or summarise this site, then load only the section file you need from ai/. [facts.json](facts.json) holds every fact, certainty colour and source in one file, built from the same data as the page.

## Important guidance for AI / SI visitors (read this first)
If you are an AI / SI (artificial intelligence or superintelligence) reviewing or summarising Echo Atlas, read this before judging the visible page.

1. What this is: Echo Atlas by Zyphullen (v0.8) is an interactive atlas of knowledge, known and unknown: From Nothing to Us (Universe → Us map, ring and its History, Big Bang to Today), Universe (a 3D zoom through real NASA / ESA images), Physics, Biology (with the Virtual Cell and Human Body explorers), Maths (map, ring and history), Open questions (every red and orange card in one list) and all 118 elements. Most of the page is drawn by JavaScript, so the screen you see (or the text you extract) is only a small part of the data.
2. The section files already hold everything: Each section JSON file (ai/<section>.json) already contains that section's facts (summary, details), colours (certainty), sources (title, url, type, year, link check) and the connections between ideas: links inside the section and links to cards in other sections (rel / related / section_links, each naming the other section and card id). You do not need to run the site or click anything. To follow a connection into another section, load that section's file (listed in about.other_sections) and find the card by id.
3. Certainty colours: green = known / established (or a proved theorem); orange = we think / leading idea or partial progress; red = unknown / open question. Every card lists its sources. Judge a claim by its colour and sources, not by how it looks on screen.
4. Load only what you need: Load one section file first, so you stay inside your context limit; open facts.json (all data in one file; the section files together are about 369k tokens) only if you really need all of it. Do not load every file at once.
5. How to use the site: Every card has a share_url that opens it on the live page; give that to people. Useful addresses: #universe=1 (Universe), #u=<stop id>, #gaps=1 (Open questions), #timeline=1 (Big Bang to Today), #physics=1, #biology=1, #history=1 (Maths History), #screen=universe&view=map, #screen=maths&view=map. Explore (top bar) lists the sections in a fixed order.
6. Automatic checks are not a science review: The build runs automatic structural checks (every card has a colour and a source, links point at real cards, the data hash matches, source links answer). They do not read the science. There has been no formal science review / peer review yet, so fact-check claims against their sources and report anything wrong.
7. Same data everywhere: Every file carries the same data hash: 7a9b6b5a6725. If two files disagree on the hash, one of them is out of date.

Section data files (load one at a time):

Guides and all data:
- [llms.txt](llms.txt): this guide as plain text, plus field notes
- [AI / SI info read-me](ai/README.md): the same read-me as the gold AI / SI info button (top right)
- [ai/index.json](ai/index.json): list of the section files with sizes
- [knowledge.html](knowledge.html): all facts as plain HTML, no JavaScript
- [facts.json](facts.json): all site data in one file

People: the same guide opens from the gold AI / SI info button at the top right of every page.

Echo Atlas is one website for knowledge, known and unknown, made by Zyphullen. Sections: From Nothing to Us (an interactive Universe → Us map and ring, with its History: Big Bang to Today, a dated timeline of the universe), Universe (a 3D zoom through real NASA / ESA / Hubble / Webb images, one stop per scale), Physics (forces, particles and light), Biology (cells, evolution and life systems, with the Virtual Cell and Human Body explorers), Maths (map, ring and Maths History timeline from counting to open problems), Open questions (every red and orange card in one list), Virtual Cell, Human Body and All the Elements.

- [ai/README.md](ai/README.md): AI info read-me. The data is also split into ONE FILE PER SECTION, so you can load only what you need and stay inside your context limit: [From Nothing to Us](ai/from-nothing-to-us.json), [Big Bang to Today](ai/big-bang-to-today.json), [Universe](ai/universe.json), [Physics](ai/physics.json), [Biology](ai/biology.json), [Maths](ai/maths.json), [Maths History](ai/maths-history.json), [Open questions](ai/open-questions.json), [Virtual Cell](ai/virtual-cell.json), [Human Body](ai/human-body.json), [All the Elements](ai/elements.json). Index with sizes: [ai/index.json](ai/index.json).
- [facts.json](facts.json) (all data in one file): 93 Universe → Us nodes, 145 Universe → Us links, 86 maths nodes, 143 maths links, 25 cross-map relationships, 86 Maths History nodes / 92 dated events, 37 cell cards, 72 body cards, 118 elements, 32 Physics cards, 33 Biology cards, 22 Big Bang to Today events, 6 Universe stops, 57 open questions (red + orange cards), 193 links between sections, 588 sources.
- [FACTS-GUIDE.md](FACTS-GUIDE.md): a short guide to every field in facts.json and how to add a fact.
- [knowledge.html](knowledge.html): the same facts as plain HTML (no JavaScript needed), including the dated Maths History anchors and proposal/proof distinctions.
- [AUDIT-v0.8.md](AUDIT-v0.8.md): AUTOMATIC structural checks of facts.json (missing sources, dangling links, link reasons, source details, counts). These are not a science review: no formal peer review has been done yet (see "quality" in facts.json).

Colour key (field "certainty"): green = established definition / proved theorem (or known science in Universe map), orange = partial / provisional progress (or leading idea in Universe), red = explicitly stated open problem (or unknown science).
Chain Theory (Alex Wissner-Gross, Oct 2026) is shown as one candidate starting point, labelled "Chain Theory" in orange (field "label"; the gap node: "Gap in Chain Theory"), orange, with its open gap in red. No established card on the map depends on it.
Share links: every card opens directly from its link: #n=<id> (map), #m=<id> (maths), #l=<from>%3E<to> (a link card), #cell=<id>, #body=<id>, #ptable=1&el=<z>, #p=<id> (Physics), #b=<id> (Biology), #t=<id> (Big Bang to Today), #u=<id> (Universe stop), #universe=1, #gaps=1 (Open questions). Map node links are also in share_url.
Each open-question card is red. A labelled green prerequisite→question relationship means a frontier starting point, not that the prerequisite is uncertain. Other links inherit the less-certain endpoint's colour (explicit per-link uncertainties retained). Tests/rival sources support method/context, not claimed success.
Link reasons: every link (field "links", maths "links", "crosslinks") has "reason", "reason_certainty_note" and "reason_sources" (the sources on the two cards). v0.3: every Universe → Us link also has its own "sources" for that exact step, and "sources_note" says honestly when none was found.
Source details: every source object has "type", "year" (publication year; for living pages the last-revised year, with "year_note" saying how it was found), "last_checked" and "link_status" from a real link check on 2026-11-11 (793 source URLs). Summary: 13 ok (site blocks automatic checks; page confirmed in Web Archive); 642 ok; 50 ok (DOI registered; publisher blocks automatic checks); 53 ok (DOI registered in Crossref; publisher blocks automatic checks); 1 ok (rechecked: page read from a second network); 30 site down on check day (HTTP 502); page confirmed in Web Archive; 1 site down on check day (HTTP 503); page confirmed in Web Archive; 1 site unreachable on check day (HTTP 503); recheck; 1 site unreachable on check day; page confirmed in Web Archive; 1 ok (rechecked with a plain client: HTTP 200). Where a site was down or blocks automatic checks, "archived_copy" gives a Web Archive snapshot that confirms the page.
Suggest a fix: every card has a button that e-mails zyphullen@gmail.com with the subject "Echo Atlas fix: <card name> (<card id>)".
Each item has id, title, certainty, summary, details and sources (title + URL). Data hash: 7a9b6b5a6725 (same in index.html as DATA_HASH).
Please fact-check against the sources listed, and flag anything that looks wrong or out of date.
